note: Placeholder authored text (owner review pending). The teacher's lessons: meet, colours, told_ward, hidden_ward, world.

lines: So you have found us. I am {name}. I teach what little magic this valley still remembers.
These people go about their work whether you help or not. Magic is how you answer the world back, and it is worth learning properly.
Ask, and I will teach you.
You broke my Ward. That is what a fracture is: the right colour in the right place, and every place broken.
Next, a fair fight. Mine will be hidden, and so will yours.
You did not break it, though I told you what it was. Remember: fracture is the right colour in the right place; echo is the right colour in the wrong place; fade is neither.
Try again whenever you like, or move on. The lesson counts either way.
Broken, and fairly. You read the echoes well. That is the whole craft: guess, listen, and guess better.
My Ward held, or yours fell first. Either way you have fought a hidden Ward, and that is the lesson. Fight me again whenever you want practice.
You have the basics. Magic is not only for duels, though: walk through the village and listen to people.
You have broken a Ward I named aloud. Now try one you cannot see.
You know your three colours. Try your hand against my Ward when you are ready.
What would you like to learn?
Three colours to begin: Flame, which burns; Frost, which stills; Vine, which binds.

In a duel each wizard hides a Ward of three places, each filled with one colour. You cast a weave of three, one colour to a place. Fracture: right colour, right place. Echo: right colour, wrong place. Fade: neither.
Flame also works in the world now. Stand close to a tree or a building and click it to burn it. Be sure of your target; fire does not ask twice.

choices.text: Let me try to break your Ward. You tell me what it is.
lines: My Ward is Frost, Vine, Frost. I will not change it. Break it in as few casts as you can.

choices.text: Fight me properly, with hidden Wards.
lines: Mine is hidden now, and yours is hidden from me. We cast until one Ward breaks.

choices.text: Is anyone in the village in need of help?
lines: Not help like a spell. Trouble like a quarrel. A hen-keeper and a carter at the end of the lane have not spoken since midsummer, and everyone around them has taken a side.
Go and hear it from them. Look for the figures with a golden mark over their heads, a little way from the centre of the village.
Walk well. Come back when you want another lesson.

opening: You have walked three days, and the valley opens below you: timber houses, smoke, a road, people already at work. None of them were waiting for you.
A wizard here is not a ruler. You cannot command these people and they will not stop for you. But you can walk among them, listen, and answer what you find with magic.
Near the road, someone in a teacher's grey is standing as if expecting you. Walk up to them and press E, or click them and choose Talk.
